text:
The suspect should be found not guilty if the jury believes his account, because the statute bars using force to resist a known arrest but still allows reasonable self-defense against an officer’s excessive force, and a punch to stop an unprovoked nightstick beating fits that privilege. He should be found guilty if the jury believes the officer, because that account has him striking first to resist arrest. The legality of the underlying arrest does not change either result under this statute.

CONFIDENCE: 74
